payload.title: Parallel sessions timeline example (examples/timeline)
payload.description:
## Intent
As someone running several coding agents at once, I want a picture of my parallel sessions over time, so that I can see how much work ran concurrently, where it overlapped, and how sessions fanned out into sub-agents.

A new example consumer, `examples/timeline`, like the meter, sentiment and privacy examples: it imports only `botspy` and std, reads sessions through the public API, and writes **one self-contained local HTML page** (inline SVG and CSS, no external scripts or network).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Agent session files] --> B[BotSpy sources / unified schema]
  B --> C[Activity model: active stretches per session]
  C --> D[Concurrency series]
  C --> E[Swimlanes by project, nested spawns]
  D --> F[timeline.html - local file]
  E --> F
```

## The picture
- **Top:** sessions active at once over time (the concurrency curve).
- **Below:** one swimlane per session, grouped by project; bars are active stretches with breaks where the session went idle; spawned sub-agents and forks nest under their parent lane.
- Agents distinguished by label **and** pattern, never colour alone (colour-blind readers). Light and dark themes. Hover shows times and message counts.

## Data it uses
Message timestamps (when the agent records them), agent, project id, started/last-activity times, and the session graph (parent / spawned-by). Sessions with no message timestamps fall back to one started..last-activity span, visibly marked as approximate.

## Not included
- No change to the core library, CLI verbs, or store.
- No server, no live updating, no publishing.
- Titles and message text are **off by default** (they can hold sensitive material); `--titles` opts in. No message text ever.

## Definition of done
All stories' scenarios pass in `cargo test --test bdd`; the example runs on the committed synthetic corpus and on a generated parallel-sessions demo corpus; README and `docs/sensitive-data.md` document it; a screenshot from synthetic data only is in the README.
